criteria_results.text: A signed development build runs on a physical iPhone and verifies pairing, isolation failures, chat/SSE/PTY, approvals, every Tool, revocation, and background recovery; committed evidence uses only a non-sensitive model label, never a device UDID.
criteria_results.notes: A locally Xcode-signed development-variant standalone app installed and launched on an iPhone 13 mini, but Google sign-in stopped at the explicit runtime guard because the build shell had no EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MOBILE_CLIENT_ID or matching redirect URI. The built bundle inspection confirmed that neither OAuth value was embedded. The real Google iOS client remains an existing human release prerequisite in #1198/#1199, so this failure does not contradict a passing physical-device claim.

process_issues.description: The ad hoc Xcode standalone build proved Apple signing and device launch but bypassed the repository-owned EAS release environment, so it could not supply the separately provisioned Google iOS OAuth client configuration.
process_issues.detected_by: Physical-device error plus secret-safe inspection of the build shell, local env-key names, and embedded Metro bundle.

failure_output: Physical iPhone: Google mobile client ID is not configured.
suggested_follow_up: Complete existing #1198/#1199 prerequisites: provision or reveal the real Google iOS OAuth client and matching reverse-client redirect through secure local/EAS configuration, configure the isolated API with the same pair, then rebuild the exact reviewed source and rerun sign-in before the remaining physical-device matrix. Do not invent, commit, or print the client configuration.
